comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained articulation; pr-1690 mounts a bicycle tire bead into a rim while avoiding tube damage.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench counterholding so jam-nut torque does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and lever-actuated cycling. pr-1690 requires bimanual bead depression into the drop center and controlled rolling of a deformable tire section over the flange.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate grades retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, repeated return accuracy, limited drift, and hands-off clearance. pr-1690 grades bead seating, valve alignment, hand clearance, partial bead-channel progress, and leak/pinch avoidance; its versions provide numeric thresholds.
comparison.reason: The objectives, manipulated mechanisms, force-control problem, and observable outcomes test meaningfully different abilities; shared bimanual coordination is only a generic primitive.
